East by Ngo Thanh Hoa – A Solid 4-Star Experience
May 2025 • Friends
1. Home Sweet Home Cocktail: A delightful blend of tamarind with balanced tangy, citrusy, and sweet notes. I only wish it was served colder, as the open kitchen seating made the area quite warm.

2. Xôi Chiên: Topped with aromatic sarsaparilla leaves, this dish offers a mochi-like texture with a savory, salty filling and a tangy sauce. The unique leaves elevate the flavor, making it a standout.

3. Garden Salad: Served with three distinct sauces, but the salad fell short. The greens were slightly wilted, lacking the crisp freshness I expected. The heat from the open kitchen may have contributed.

4. Softshell Crab: Crunchy, tasty, and refreshing, this dish was enjoyable but not particularly innovative or surprising.

5. Prawns in Laksa Sauce: My least favorite. While the prawns were sweet and fresh, they didn’t harmonize with the sauce. The sauce itself, with a spicy satay-like kick, was flavorful but felt disconnected from the dish.

6. Five-Spice Pork Jowl: A well-balanced dish featuring tender, buttery pork jowl paired with pickled carrots, lotus root, and smashed mung bean. The tangy sauce tied everything together beautifully.

7. Five-Spice Quail: The quail itself was bland, relying heavily on an overly salty sauce for flavor. Eaten together, it’s decent but lacks a wow factor—nothing memorable.

8. New Zealand Toothfish: The highlight of the night. Perfectly cooked fish soaked in a spicy miso sauce, complemented by a refreshing orange and grapefruit salad. Easily my favorite.

9. Dessert: Hương Quê Ice Cream: relatively good especially when the surrounding was getting warm.

Overall: East delivers a solid 4-star upscale dining experience but falls short of true modern fine dining. Serving a salad with three sauces doesn’t qualify as innovative, nor does it creatively challenge the palate like modern cuisine should. My favorites were the xôi chiên and the toothfish. The salad disappointed due to wilted greens, and the laksa prawns lacked cohesion. Other dishes were pleasant but unremarkable. Sitting near the open kitchen offers a lively view of the action, but the heat can be uncomfortable—something to keep in mind.

Sydney barista to Saigon chef
Apr 2024 • Solo
I must be honest, I know Harold from his time when he lived in Sydney. But I knew him then as a barista - a very good barista.

But now, after not seeing him for a dozen or so years, I now can say I know him a a very very good chef!!

He may have been Vietnam’s inaugural MasterChef winner, but since that acclaim he has obviously studied and refined his style and techniques thereby establishing himself as a leading chef and restaurateur in Saigon.

His modern approach to Vietnamese cuisine while always using fresh local produce accompanied often with Australian and other Pacific Rim protein shows both his Heritage and his understanding of modern Australian cooking.

I thoroughly enjoyed his degustation menu interpretations finding all his cooking techniques, flavours and textures to be world class. I enjoyed seeing him again ‘working the kitchen pass’ and obviously revelling in his new role as chef/owner of his own restaurant.

New and Great Dining Spot
Dec 2022
We happened to stumble upon this place whilst going to the Chua Xa Loi Buddist Pagoda on the same street and after a brief chat with the very friendly owner Mr. Ngo Thanh Hoa, we booked dinner for 30.12.2022.

The restaurant itself is very new (we believe it opened only three weeks beforehand) with very slick and contemporary interior. The ground floor is an open bar with seating facing the kitchen which is on full display although there are other rooms in the next level or two We chose to sit at the bar as we love to see how the team works in a kitchen.

The food was very good and features a lot of Australian produce meat wise as well as in the wine list. We started off with cocktails which were excellent before staring our entrees; the "Luori bo nurong" (grilled beef tongue) for me and the ""So diep ap chao" (Pan seared scallop) for my wife and both of each were lovely and a correct proportion for an entree in order to whet the appetite for mains!

For mains I chose the "Ma bo ham" (slow cooked beef check) whilst my wife had the "Ca tuyet ap chap" (Pan fried tooth fish) and both where again excellent and then my wife had the "Chuoi nurong" (Grilled banana) for desert which was a light way to finish.

At the end of the meal our host cracked open a bottle of rather nice looking Japanese whisky and treated us to a few drinks which was very generous!

It's not the cheapest place in HCMC but to our minds was well worth the money for a lovely evening out so we hope that this place success as it would be well deserved.
